import pandas as pd

# Load the timeseries catalog and values for the zone
catalog = pd.read_csv(CATALOG_CSV)
power_id = catalog[catalog['point_uri'] == 'https://buildsys.org/uuid/B85B166C-04BD-3799-ABB4-47CFDB3AFA52']['timeseries_id'].iloc[0]
occupancy_id = catalog[catalog['point_uri'] == 'https://buildsys.org/uuid/C14E13FF-6D23-3DDE-9E51-056A89A59BDE']['timeseries_id'].iloc[0]

def load_series(series_id):
    values = pd.read_csv(VALUES_CSV)
    return values[values['timeseries_id'] == series_id][['timestamp', 'value']]  # Keep only timestamp and value columns

power_series = load_series(power_id)
power_series['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(power_series['timestamp'])
occupancy_series = load_series(occupancy_id)
occupancy_series['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(occupancy_series['timestamp'])

# Filter for date '2018-07-23' and unoccupied state
power_series = power_series[(power_series['timestamp'].dt.date == pd.to_datetime('2018-07-23').date()) &
                              (power_series['value'] > 1)]
occupancy_series = occupancy_series[(occupancy_series['timestamp'].dt.date == pd.to_datetime('2018-07-23').date()) &
                                      (occupancy_series['value'] == 0)]

# Align time series on timestamps
joined_series = power_series.set_index('timestamp').join(
    occupancy_series.set_index('timestamp'),
    lsuffix='_power', rsuffix='_occupancy')

# Calculate hours where lights are on and zone is unoccupied
hours_on_while_unoccupied = joined_series['value_power'].notna().sum()

print(hours_on_while_unoccupied)
